Girard | Lecture {{< meta lecture >}}]{} ::: ![](../../img/proud_coder_357EDD.svg){.absolute bottom=30 right=0 width="400"} ::: ## Roadmap ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Understand the principles of relational data and keys - Conceptually differentiate mutating join types - Perform joins in R using {dplyr} functions ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/map.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: # Relational Data ## Relational Data {.fs70} - A set of inter-related tables is called a *relational database* (RDB) ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
user movie rating
sing.it.sam 1 ★☆☆☆☆
sing.it.sam 2 ★★★★★
macattack 1 ★★★★☆
macattack 2 ★★☆☆☆
inzain99 1 ★★★☆☆
inzain99 2 ★★☆☆☆
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [users]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
user fname lname
sing.it.sam Sam Jones
macattack Alex Mackey
inzain99 Zain Baker
````` ::: ::: [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
id title year genre
1 John Wick 2 2017 Action
2 Frozen II 2019 Family
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Relational Data {.fs70} - To **join** the tables into one unified dataset, we need to know their connections ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
user fname lname movie title year genre rating
sing.it.sam Sam Jones 1 John Wick 2 2017 Action ★☆☆☆☆
sing.it.sam Sam Jones 2 Frozen II 2019 Family ★★★★★
macattack Alex Mackey 1 John Wick 2 2017 Action ★★★★☆
macattack Alex Mackey 2 Frozen II 2019 Family ★★☆☆☆
inzain99 Zain Baker 1 John Wick 2 2017 Action ★★★☆☆
inzain99 Zain Baker 2 Frozen II 2019 Family ★★☆☆☆
````` ::: ::: ## Keys {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} - Data is [relational]{.b .blue} when one observation references another observation - Each observation needs to be uniquely identified by one or more variables - These variables are called "keys" - [Natural keys]{.b .green} are meaningful - e.g., `users$user` - [Surrogate keys]{.b .green} are meaningless - e.g., `movies$id` - The ratings table has a double-key ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} ![](../../img/keys.png) ::: ::: ## Complex Databases {.fs60} - Let's try to guess the connections for the {nycflights13} package's tables ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} ![](../../img/flights1.png) ::: ::: {.column .tc .fragment width="50%"} ![](../../img/flights2.png) ::: ::: # Basic Join Types ## Basic Join Types {.fs70} - The basic joins handle non-overlapping or missing observations differently ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| year| |-----:|----:| | 1| 2020| | 2| 2003| | 3| 2019| | 4| 2006| | 5| 2003| | 6| 2002| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [avg_ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| average| |-----:|-------:| | 2| 2.2| | 3| 8.0| | 4| 6.7| | 5| 8.7| | 6| 3.5| | 7| 7.5| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="15%"} ::: ::: {.column width="35%"} ![](../../img/joins.png) ::: ::: ## Left Join {.fs70} ::: {} - Left join includes all rows in the [left] table; those missing in the [right] table get NA ::: ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| year| |-----:|----:| | 1| 2020| | 2| 2003| | 3| 2019| | 4| 2006| | 5| 2003| | 6| 2002| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [avg_ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| average| |-----:|-------:| | 2| 2.2| | 3| 8.0| | 4| 6.7| | 5| 8.7| | 6| 3.5| | 7| 7.5| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [Left Join (movies, avg_ratings)]{.b .green} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
movie year average
1 2020 NA
2 2003 2.2
3 2019 8.0
4 2006 6.7
5 2003 8.7
6 2002 3.5
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Right Join {.fs70} ::: {} - Right join includes all rows in the [right] table; those missing in the [left] table get NA ::: ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| year| |-----:|----:| | 1| 2020| | 2| 2003| | 3| 2019| | 4| 2006| | 5| 2003| | 6| 2002| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [avg_ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| average| |-----:|-------:| | 2| 2.2| | 3| 8.0| | 4| 6.7| | 5| 8.7| | 6| 3.5| | 7| 7.5| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [Right Join (movies, avg_ratings)]{.b .green} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
movie year average
2 2003 2.2
3 2019 8.0
4 2006 6.7
5 2003 8.7
6 2002 3.5
7 NA 7.5
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Inner Join {.fs70} ::: {} - Inner join includes only rows present in both the [left] and [right] tables; no new NAs ::: ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| year| |-----:|----:| | 1| 2020| | 2| 2003| | 3| 2019| | 4| 2006| | 5| 2003| | 6| 2002| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [avg_ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| average| |-----:|-------:| | 2| 2.2| | 3| 8.0| | 4| 6.7| | 5| 8.7| | 6| 3.5| | 7| 7.5| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [Inner Join (movies, avg_ratings)]{.b .green} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
movie year average
2 2003 2.2
3 2019 8.0
4 2006 6.7
5 2003 8.7
6 2002 3.5
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Full Join {.fs70} ::: {} - Full join includes all rows in either the [left] or [right] table; missing values become NAs ::: ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [movies]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| year| |-----:|----:| | 1| 2020| | 2| 2003| | 3| 2019| | 4| 2006| | 5| 2003| | 6| 2002| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="25%"} [avg_ratings]{.b .blue} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | movie| average| |-----:|-------:| | 2| 2.2| | 3| 8.0| | 4| 6.7| | 5| 8.7| | 6| 3.5| | 7| 7.5| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc width="50%"} [Full Join (movies, avg_ratings)]{.b .green} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
movie year average
1 2020 NA
2 2003 2.2
3 2019 8.0
4 2006 6.7
5 2003 8.7
6 2002 3.5
7 NA 7.5
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: # Tidyverse Joins ## Tidyverse Joins {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - {dplyr} has intuitive, standard names for these concepts + `left_join(x, y, by)` + `right_join(x, y, by)` + `inner_join(x, y, by)` + `full_join(x, y, by)` - It is easiest if the key variables have the same names in both tibbles + e.g., `by = "carrier"` + e.g., `by = c("user", "movie")` - But you can join by differently named keys too + e.g., `by = join_by(faa == origin)` ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/invert.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## Preparing our Data ::: {.fs80} Let's examine a subset of columns from `flights`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data("flights", package = "nycflights13") flights2 <- flights |> select(month, day, flight, origin, dest, tailnum, carrier) |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 336,776 × 7 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL # ℹ 336,771 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## The Airlines Dataset ::: {.fs80} Before we join, let's look at the `airlines` dataset. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data("airlines", package = "nycflights13") airlines ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 16 × 2 carrier name 1 9E Endeavor Air Inc. 2 AA American Airlines Inc. 3 AS Alaska Airlines Inc. 4 B6 JetBlue Airways 5 DL Delta Air Lines Inc. # ℹ 11 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Left Join in R ::: {.fs80} **Question:** *What is the full name of the airline carrier for each flight?* A left join is perfect for looking up and adding reference information to our primary dataset. Notice that the number of rows remains exactly the same. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 336,776 × 8 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier name 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA United Air Lines Inc. 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA United Air Lines Inc. 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA American Airlines Inc. 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 JetBlue Airways 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL Delta Air Lines Inc. # ℹ 336,771 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## The Airports Dataset ::: {.fs80} Next, let's select a few columns from `airports`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data("airports", package = "nycflights13") airports2 <- airports |> select(faa, name) |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1,458 × 2 faa name 1 04G Lansdowne Airport 2 06A Moton Field Municipal Airport 3 06C Schaumburg Regional 4 06N Randall Airport 5 09J Jekyll Island Airport # ℹ 1,453 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Joining by Different Names ::: {.fs80} If the key variables are named differently across datasets, we provide `by` with the `join_by()` function. The order should match `first == second`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> left_join(airports2, by = join_by(origin == faa)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 336,776 × 8 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier name 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA Newark Liberty Intl 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA La Guardia 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA John F Kennedy Intl 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 John F Kennedy Intl 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL La Guardia # ℹ 336,771 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Duplicate Column Names ::: {.fs80} We now have the name.x (origin) and name.y (dest)... ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> left_join(airports2, by = join_by(origin == faa)) |> left_join(airports2, by = join_by(dest == faa)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 336,776 × 9 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier name.x name.y 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA Newark Liberty Intl George Bu… 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA La Guardia George Bu… 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA John F Kennedy Intl Miami Intl 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 John F Kennedy Intl 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL La Guardia Hartsfiel… # ℹ 336,771 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Changing the Suffixes ::: {.fs80} We can replace ".x" and ".y" using `suffix` in the second join. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> left_join(airports2, by = join_by(origin == faa)) |> left_join(airports2, by = join_by(dest == faa), suffix = c("_origin", "_dest")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 336,776 × 9 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier name_origin name_dest 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA Newark Liberty Intl George Bu… 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA La Guardia George Bu… 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA John F Kennedy Intl Miami Intl 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 John F Kennedy Intl 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL La Guardia Hartsfiel… # ℹ 336,771 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## The Planes Dataset ::: {.fs80} Finally, let's select a few columns from `planes`. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data("planes", package = "nycflights13") planes2 <- planes |> select(tailnum, manufacturer, model) |> print() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3,322 × 3 tailnum manufacturer model 1 N10156 EMBRAER EMB-145XR 2 N102UW AIRBUS INDUSTRIE A320-214 3 N103US AIRBUS INDUSTRIE A320-214 4 N104UW AIRBUS INDUSTRIE A320-214 5 N10575 EMBRAER EMB-145LR # ℹ 3,317 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Missing Matches ::: {.fs80} If `flights2` has a key that does not exist in the right dataset, the joined variables become `NA`. Let's look at plane "N3ALAA" to see this in action. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> left_join(planes2, by = "tailnum") |> filter(tailnum == "N3ALAA") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 63 × 9 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier manufacturer model 1 1 1 301 LGA ORD N3ALAA AA 2 1 2 353 LGA ORD N3ALAA AA 3 1 3 301 LGA ORD N3ALAA AA 4 1 7 359 LGA ORD N3ALAA AA 5 1 8 1351 JFK ORD N3ALAA AA # ℹ 58 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Inner Join in R ::: {.fs80} **Question:** *Which flights were flown by planes that we have registry data for?* To only return rows that have a match in both tables, use inner join. Our row count will decrease because it drops flights with missing plane data. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> inner_join(planes2, by = "tailnum") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 284,170 × 9 month day flight origin dest tailnum carrier manufacturer model 1 1 1 1545 EWR IAH N14228 UA BOEING 737-824 2 1 1 1714 LGA IAH N24211 UA BOEING 737-824 3 1 1 1141 JFK MIA N619AA AA BOEING 757-223 4 1 1 725 JFK BQN N804JB B6 AIRBUS A320-232 5 1 1 461 LGA ATL N668DN DL BOEING 757-232 # ℹ 284,165 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Right Join in R ::: {.fs80} **Question:** *Which airports in our data received zero flights from NYC in 2013?* A right join is useful when we want to keep all observations from a reference table on the right without breaking the flow of our code. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> right_join(airports2, by = join_by(dest == faa)) |> filter(is.na(flight)) |> select(dest, name) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1,357 × 2 dest name 1 04G Lansdowne Airport 2 06A Moton Field Municipal Airport 3 06C Schaumburg Regional 4 06N Randall Airport 5 09J Jekyll Island Airport # ℹ 1,352 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Full Join in R ::: {.fs80} **Question:** *Overall, how many flights went to unlisted airports, and how many listed airports received zero flights?* A full join keeps *all* rows from both tables. By joining flights with airports, we can audit the overlaps and missing matches across our entire database. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} flights2 |> full_join(airports2, by = join_by(dest == faa)) |> count( missing_airport = is.na(name), missing_flight = is.na(flight) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 missing_airport missing_flight n 1 FALSE FALSE 329174 2 FALSE TRUE 1357 3 TRUE FALSE 7602 ``` ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
